title: साङ्ख्या दर्शनको कोणबाट राजेश्वर देवकोटाका उपन्यासको विश्लेषण
nepali: प्रस्तुत लेख राजेश्वर देवकोटाका उपन्यासका कथावस्तुमा साङ्ख्य दर्शन खोज्नमा केन्द्रित रहेको छ । कथावस्तुमा साङ्ख्य दर्शनका मूल तत्व प्रकृति, पुरुष र नैतिकता खोज्ने काम भएको छ । पुरुषका निष्पृहता, निस्क्रियता, ज्ञानात्मकता जस्ता विशेषता र प्रकृतिका मोहात्मकता, अनित्यता र परिवर्तनशीलता जस्ता लक्षण कथावस्तुमा छन् भन्ने देखाइएको छ । विश्लेषणका क्रममा देवकोटाका आठवटा औपन्यासिक कृतिमध्ये चारवटा कृति मात्र शीर्षकअनुसार समावेश हुन सकेका छन् । कृतिको विश्लेषणका लागि छोटोमा सैद्धान्तिक आधार प्रस्तुत गरेर कृतिगत तथ्यबाट त्यसलाई जाँच्ने काम गरिएको छ । विश्लेषणात्मक अध्ययनपछि साङ्ख्य दर्शनको प्रभावका दृष्टिले बढी महŒवको कृति पूर्वकथा हो भन्ने निष्कर्ष दिइएको छ । , , , , ,
american_english: The present article is centered on looking for Sāṃkhya philosophy in the plots of Rajeshwar Devkota's novels. An attempt has been made to locate the fundamental elements of Sāṃkhya philosophy — prakṛti, puruṣa and morality — in the plots. It is shown that the plots contain characteristics of puruṣa such as dispassion, inactivity and consciousness, and traits of prakṛti such as delusion, impermanence and mutability. In the course of analysis, only four out of Devkota's eight novelistic works could be included, according to the title. For the analysis of the works, a theoretical basis has been presented briefly, and it has been examined through the facts of the works. After the analytical study, the conclusion has been put forward that, from the standpoint of the influence of Sāṃkhya philosophy, the work of greater significance is Purvakatha.
british_english: The present article is centred upon the search for Sāṃkhya philosophy in the plots of Rajeshwar Devkota's novels. An endeavour has been made to locate the fundamental elements of Sāṃkhya philosophy — prakṛti, puruṣa and morality — within the plots. It is shown that the plots exhibit characteristics of puruṣa such as dispassion, inertia and consciousness, and traits of prakṛti such as infatuation, impermanence and mutability. In the course of the analysis, of Devkota's eight novelistic works only four — corresponding to the title — could be included. For the purpose of analysing the works, a theoretical basis has been set out briefly, and thereafter it has been examined against the facts of the works themselves. Following the analytical study, the conclusion has been drawn that, from the standpoint of the influence of Sāṃkhya philosophy, the work of greater significance is Purvakatha.
